name: Ventrue of Note (Libellus Sanguinis I Lore)

pages.name: Alexander, Ruler of the Grand Court

text.content:
A @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} elder of the early feudal period, Alexander founded the Grand Court of Paris in cooperation with @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} elders after the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue}-@UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} alliance that had backed Charlemagne collapsed into open warfare following the empire's fragmentation. For generations he ruled the Grand Court effectively, holding the fragile clan truce together through sheer force of will and political acumen — until the tragedy of Lorraine broke him utterly.

After torturing his obsession to death and losing the mystical rose into which he had poured her draining vitae and soul, Alexander descended into madness and grief, and the Grand Court languished for a generation under ineffective @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} stewardship before the mysterious Countess Saviarre arrived to restore its function in his name. Alexander nominally still rules the Grand Court, but it is Saviarre who truly wields its power, and few outside the innermost circle know how complete his broken dependence on her has become. The recent awakening of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} elder Mithras in England has begun to destabilize the already-fragile Ventrue/Toreador balance he built, and many fear the Grand Court's final collapse is now only a matter of time.

Lorraine was a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} neonate whom the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} elders of the Grand Court gifted to Alexander as a political concession, hoping to bind the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} ruler more closely to their interests. She remained politely, unreachably distant despite his growing devotion. When a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} broodmate became equally obsessed with her and abducted her outright, Alexander hunted the abductor down and destroyed him — then turned his fury and heartbreak on Lorraine herself, torturing her to death over seven nights. In her final act he drained her blood and, by means known only to himself, her very soul into the petals of a single white rose, meaning to possess her essence forever. Her last words to him were "I love you."

The ordeal shattered Alexander's mind, and in his madness the rose vanished. Its whereabouts, and the rumored powers it may grant whoever possesses Lorraine's soul, remain a mystery the Toreador pursue to this day — and some among the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} whisper that Countess Saviarre's uncannily rapid rise to Alexander's total trust may not be unconnected to the rose's disappearance.

Countess Saviarre arrived at the Grand Court of Paris in the eleventh century, seemingly from nowhere, at the height of its decline under Alexander's grief-broken rule and the ineffective @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} stewardship that followed. Within a remarkably short span she won Alexander's total and unquestioning trust, and through him restored the Grand Court's function as the seat of French Cainite politics — a recovery so swift and so complete that many @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} alike suspect supernatural means behind it, whether a blood oath sworn over the broken elder or, more darkly, possession of Lorraine's lost rose and the soul it is said to contain. Saviarre neither confirms nor denies these rumors, and rules the Grand Court in Alexander's name with a competence that leaves little room to challenge her position, whatever its true source.

pages.name: Mithras, the Awakened Elder of England

text.content: Long before the Norman Conquest, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} in the Duchy of Normandy taught the Norman dukes statecraft and unified the region's Cainites under their command; after 1066 Norman @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} spread across England "like an aristocratic plague," eliminating or subjugating the island's earlier mixed population of @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador}, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra}, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian}, and Scottish @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel} Kindred and coming to dominate the English Church and nobility. Mithras is the ancient @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} elder whose recent awakening in England now stands atop that conquest — his return already rippling outward to destabilize the fragile Ventrue/@UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} balance so carefully maintained at the Grand Court of Paris. Across the Narrow Sea, Mithras has also turned his attention to Glastonbury, where he has so far failed to oust the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} witch Meerlinda from her hold on the site, a standing rebuke to his authority that many expect him to answer with force in time.

pages.name: Meerlinda, the Witch of Glastonbury (Tremere Cross-Reference)

text.content: Though Meerlinda is @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} rather than @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue}, her presence looms over @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} affairs in the British Isles. Most Patricians regard the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} as dangerous upstarts, resented for their willingness to practice amaranth against elders and for the rigid, threatening organization the new clan has built in only a few generations — sentiment enough that many @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} believe the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} should be exterminated before they multiply further. It is against this backdrop that Meerlinda has established herself at Glastonbury, resisting every attempt by the Ventrue elder Mithras to oust her from the site. Her continued defiance is a rare and pointed check on Ventrue power in England, and a reminder that the clan's hostility toward the Tremere is, for now, more sentiment than accomplished fact.
